data.title: Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc. Receives Nasdaq Minimum Bid Price Deficiency Notice
data.description:
NANCHANG, China, Oct. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc. (the "Company") today announced that it received a written notice dated October 7, 2026 from Nasdaq stating that the closing bid price of its ordinary shares was below $1.00 per share for 30 consecutive business days, from August 25 through October 6, 2026. Accordingly, the Company does not meet the minimum bid price requirement for continued listing on the Nasdaq Capital Market under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5550(a)(2).

Under Nasdaq Listing Rule 5810(c)(3)(A), the Company has 180 calendar days, until April 5, 2027, to regain compliance. Compliance requires a closing bid price of at least $1.00 per share for a minimum of ten consecutive business days during that period, subject to Nasdaq's discretion to require a longer period and its written confirmation.

The notice has no immediate effect on the listing or trading of the Company's ordinary shares on the Nasdaq Capital Market.

About Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc.

Ruanyun Edai Technology Inc. is an AI-driven education technology company focused on intelligent content recognition, automated assessment and next-generation learning systems. The Company has historically developed and provided AI-enabled teaching, learning and assessment solutions, including smart homework, smart examination and digital education services, and since September 2025 has provided campus operations and student-life services through its Smart Campus Services business.

The Company is presenting its group businesses under the Formind Group identity as part of its broader strategy to expand AI education, language learning, institutional education support and global technology initiatives. Additional information about Formind Group is available at www.formind.group. Information on that website is not part of this press release.

data.title: Humana Stock Surges After Key Medicare Advantage Plan Gets Higher Rating — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Catherine Dunn

Humana stock gained 11.56% Friday after the federal government released new ratings data on Medicare Advantage plans, showing that Humana increased its membership in four-star rated plans, a key metric closely watched by Wall Street.

Shares ended the session at $431.87, Humana's highest close since Jan. 17, 2024, when they ended the day at $447.76, according to Dow Jones Market Data.

After a sharp fall two years ago, the insurer was looking to make a comeback on the new 2027 ratings, which were anticipated this week. The ratings are tied to financial bonuses in the Medicare Advantage program, and Humana's results were expected to test the stock, which had already soared this year. It's now up more than 68% year to date, versus 14% for the broader market.

Humana made big strides in the latest ratings round. The company said 95% of its members are now enrolled in plans rated four stars or higher, up from 45% earlier this year.

In a securities filing Friday morning, Humana said it is "well positioned to deliver on its commitment of unlocking the earnings potential of the business by 2028."

"Bottom Line: HUM...is the clearest positive big winner in our 2027 Stars analysis," Leerink Partners said in a client note.

As seniors begin to shop for Medicare health coverage this month, the rating system is meant to help them compare the quality of plans, on a scale of one to five stars.

For insurers and Wall Street, star ratings are an incredibly important metric because they determine quality bonus payments to insurers from the government. Plans rated four stars and above are eligible for the bonuses. This year alone, those bonus payments are expected to total more than $13 billion in aggregate.

At Humana, "getting the quality bonus payment back on some of their large contracts is empirical to the margin recovery story," Leerink Partners analyst Whit Mayo told Barron's in an interview this week. "That's the primary investment thesis for investors."

The challenge for Humana started two years ago, when the insurer saw a ratings drop, and went from having more than 90% of its members in a plan rated at least four stars, down to about 25%. At the time, Humana said it had narrowly missed thresholds on a small number of measures used to calculate stars. That reduction impacted Humana's ability to collect bonuses this year.

When the 2026 ratings were announced last year, the results continued to show a gap between Humana and industry peers CVS Health and UnitedHealth Group, each with more than 80% of their members in plans with four or more stars this year, according to Leerink.

On Thursday, both CVS Health and UnitedHealth Group saw some decline in that measure for 2027, with about 70% of each company's membership in a four-star or higher plan next year, a Leerink analysis found.

A UnitedHealth spokesperson said the new star ratings "are in line with our expectations and reflect our continued investment in improving members' health outcomes."

CVS Health's Aetna insurance arm, in a statement, said the results position the company as a high performer "for the third consecutive year and highlight strong performance across various clinical quality, preventive care and member experience measures."

CVS shares lost 1.87% Friday, closing at $86.16, while UnitedHealth stock rose 2.25%, for a closing price of $379.30.

Alignment Healthcare, which said Thursday that a California HMO contract received a 3.5-star rating for 2027, tumbled more than 13% Friday, to $7.55 at market close. In a statement, the company said it "believes the rating does not accurately reflect the contract's longstanding performance on evidence-based measures of quality, clinical outcomes and member experience."

Humana was aiming for a boost in 2027 stars, which translate to bonus payments in 2028. Improving the ratings wasn't going to be an overnight fix. Stars are based on 40-some criteria that encompass patient experience surveys and a range of care metrics.

During Humana's last earnings call in July, CEO James Rechtin said he felt good about the company's "operational progress," adding that the company was driven "to be closing every single gap we possibly can..."

The insurer is "very focused on consumer engagement," said Mayo. Efforts to lift ratings are "probably one of the most important initiatives that Humana has had for two years."

A question for Wall Street was just how much the company needed to improve this time around, particularly when it came to one of its largest Medicare Advantage contracts, known as H5216. That contract ultimately moved up to a four-star rating, new data show.

Write to Catherine Dunn at catherine.dunn@dowjones.com

data.title: Lockheed Martin unveils PAC-3 Edge interceptor designed to counter hypersonic threats
data.description:
Lockheed Martin on Friday unveiled PAC-3 Edge, a missile interceptor designed to defend against hypersonic and advanced missile threats, as the US military looks to strengthen its capabilities to counter emerging aerial threats.

Growing demand for air and missile defense systems amid conflicts in Ukraine and the Middle East has strained US weapons stockpiles, prompting the US Army to award Lockheed Martin a contract worth up to $58.6 billion in July to ramp up production of PAC-3 interceptors.

Lockheed Martin said PAC-3 Edge incorporates a new seeker, upgraded flight controls and a multi-pulse rocket motor supplied by Northrop Grumman, enhancing the interceptor's ability to counter advanced threats, including hypersonic missiles, at longer ranges and higher altitudes.

"The cost of this would be about that of the existing PAC-3 MSE," Tim Cahill, president of missiles and fire control at Lockheed Martin, told Reuters. "At full production, the annual rate would be about 2,000 units a year, comparable with PAC-3 MSE."

In January, Lockheed Martin signed a seven-year framework agreement with the US Department of Defense to expand production of its PAC-3 missile interceptors, aiming to increase annual manufacturing capacity to 2,000 units from about 600.

data.title: Patriot Mobile, Values-Driven Wireless Provider, Files for NASDAQ IPO
data.description:
Patriot Mobile Inc. filed for an initial public offering of its Class A common stock. The Texas-based, values-driven wireless provider plans to list on Nasdaq under the ticker “PTRT.” Northland Capital Markets is serving as the sole book-running manager.

Business Description

Patriot Mobile is a values-driven, nationwide communications company that operates an asset-light mobile virtual network operator (MVNO) model. Instead of owning spectrum or building network infrastructure, the company purchases wholesale capacity through aggregators to access all three major national wireless networks. Patriot Mobile provides postpaid wireless voice, text, and data services, connected devices, device protection, financing, mobile internet and 5G home wireless, along with accessories. The company differentiates through a mission-led brand, 100% U.S.-based customer support, and coverage flexibility that allows customers to move between supported networks if needed.

The company targets consumers, families, businesses, churches, ministries, nonprofits, and other organizations seeking to align purchasing with Christian-conservative values. Revenue is primarily subscription-based, supplemented by device and accessory sales and value-added services. Patriot Mobile emphasizes a diversified, omni-channel acquisition engine (radio/podcasts, television, digital, referrals, affiliates, sponsorships, and events) and a digital-first onboarding experience. Its strategy aims to expand wallet share with offerings like device protection and 5G home wireless, while also pursuing adjacent opportunities (e.g., insurance and other technology services) over time.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Approximately 28.3 million U.S. adults who identify as “very conservative,” equating to a core SAM of about $15 billion and an expanded opportunity of $40+ billion across adjacent services.
  • Market growth: U.S. wireless data usage reached 132 trillion MB in 2024, growing roughly 35% annually for three consecutive years.
  • Market position: Asset-light MVNO with access to all three major national wireless networks, targeting values-aligned consumers and organizations.
  • Key competitors: AT&T, Verizon, T-Mobile; MVNOs such as Consumer Cellular, Google Fi, US Mobile, MobileX, Spectrum Mobile, Xfinity Mobile, and others.
  • Industry trends: Rising postpaid churn amid competitive promotions; rapid 5G adoption; increasing demand for bundled and converged connectivity; expanding consumer preference for values-aligned brands.

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Approximately 186,000 active wireless lines as of December 31, 2025; 202,848 as of June 30, 2026
  • Locations: Headquarters in Grapevine, Texas; nationwide service footprint via multi-network access
  • Geographic presence: United States (nationwide coverage across all three major national networks)
  • Partnerships: Multi-network access via MVNAs; marketing partnerships and sponsorships including NASCAR and SEC football
  • Other key metrics: Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 86 (as of December 31, 2025); average monthly churn of ~1% in 2025; 2025 ARPU of approximately $543; 100% U.S.-based customer service; launched 5G Home Wireless to consumers in May 2026

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): $92.96 million (FY 2025)
  • Revenue growth: 24.5% year-over-year (2025 vs. 2024)
  • Gross profit: $40.82 million (FY 2025) (43.9% margin)
  • Operating income: $(1.87) million (FY 2025)
  • Net income: $(3.27) million (FY 2025)

Management

  • Glenn Story, Chief Executive Officer - Co-founder; 25+ years in strategic planning, finance and operations; non-practicing CPA; previously led businesses and finance organizations in New York.
  • Jenny Story, Chief Operating Officer - 30+ years in corporate finance and investment management with Salomon Brothers, Bankers Trust, Fitch Ratings and C-III Asset Management.
  • Justin Cordon, Chief Financial Officer - Background in private equity, investment banking and portfolio company leadership; experience in capital formation, M&A and operations.
  • Scott Coburn, Chief Marketing Officer - Former co-founder of Rev19; led marketing at a digital agency; prior leadership roles at Sabre Holdings and EDS.
  • Robert (Bob) Barracca, Chief Technology Officer - 25 years in technology leadership; previously VP of Technology at Avero; expertise in infrastructure, systems integration and scaling platforms.
  • Emily Epperson, General Counsel - Corporate attorney with experience across energy and nonprofit sectors; licensed in Texas and Illinois; focuses on governance and compliance.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: Patriot Mobile Inc.
  • Filing date: October 09, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: PTRT
  • Exchange: NASDAQ
  • Lead underwriters: Northland Capital Markets (sole book-running manager)
  • Use of proceeds: Purchase newly issued LLC Units from Patriot Mobile Holdings LLC; fund redemptions of LLC Units from certain continuing equity holders; repay borrowings under the company’s revolving line of credit; pay offering expenses; and for general corporate purposes including potential acquisitions.

data.title: Bambusa Therapeutics, Clinical-Stage Biopharma Developing Bispecific Antibodies for I&I, Files for Nasdaq Global Select Market IPO
data.description:
Bambusa Therapeutics, a clinical-stage biopharma focused on next‑generation bispecific antibodies for immunology and inflammation, filed for an initial public offering. The company has applied to list its common stock on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the symbol “BBTX.” Proceeds will support advancement of lead programs BBT001 and BBT002, pipeline development, and general corporate purposes.

Business Description

Bambusa Therapeutics is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing next‑generation, long‑acting bispecific antibodies designed to address complex immunology and inflammation (I&I) diseases. Its approach combines two validated inflammatory pathways into a single molecule, engineered for extended half‑life and high‑concentration subcutaneous delivery to improve efficacy, durability, and dosing convenience. The company’s lead program, BBT001, targets IL‑4Rα and IL‑31 for atopic dermatitis and other dermatologic conditions, with Phase 1/2 proof‑of‑concept readouts underway. BBT002 targets IL‑4Rα and IL‑5 for respiratory diseases including COPD, CRSwNP, and asthma and has shown dual biomarker effects and favorable safety in healthy volunteers. Two additional programs are in preclinical development: BBT003 (TL1A + IL‑23p19) for inflammatory bowel disease and BBT004 for autoantibody‑driven autoimmune disorders.

Bambusa leverages a clinically validated bispecific antibody architecture originating from BioNTech Zhuhai, incorporates half‑life extension technologies, and prioritizes indications with large, growing markets and unmet needs. Its strategy is to establish clinical proof‑of‑concept in focused indications and expand each asset as a “pipeline‑in‑a‑molecule” across related I&I conditions, while building the late‑stage, regulatory, and commercial capabilities needed for future launches.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Global I&I market projected to exceed $200 billion by 2030.
  • Market growth: Estimated ~6% CAGR from 2025 to 2030 in I&I.
  • Market position: Pipeline of long-acting bispecific antibodies with worldwide rights and a clinically validated scaffold; focus on dermatology, respiratory, gastroenterology, and autoimmune diseases.
  • Key competitors: Regeneron/Sanofi (Dupixent), Eli Lilly (Ebglyss), Galderma (Nemluvio), GSK (Nucala), AstraZeneca/Amgen (Tezspire), Genentech/Novartis (Xolair), Janssen, AbbVie, BMS, Takeda, among others.
  • Industry trends: Shift toward targeted biologics and multi-target bispecifics, half‑life extension for less frequent dosing, expansion of biologics into earlier lines and broader phenotypes.

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Pre-revenue; no commercial customers
  • Locations: Headquarters at 22 Boston Wharf Road, Floor 7, Boston, Massachusetts
  • Geographic presence: Clinical activity across the United States, Australia, Europe, Georgia, New Zealand, and China
  • Partnerships: Research and license agreements with BioNTech (Zhuhai); manufacturing with WuXi Biologics; optioned discovery programs and licensed BBT003/BBT004
  • Orders/GMV: Not applicable (pre-revenue clinical stage)
  • Other key metrics: 30 full-time employees as of September 30, 2026; multiple ongoing Phase 1/2 studies and additional preclinical programs targeting first-in-human by 2026–2027

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): No revenue (pre-revenue clinical-stage company)
  • Operating income: Loss from operations: $(44.0) million (2025); $(24.1) million (six months ended June 30, 2026)
  • Net income: Net loss: $(41.1) million (2025); $(22.4) million (six months ended June 30, 2026)

Management

  • Shanshan Xu, M.D., Ph.D., M.B.A., Chief Executive Officer, President, and Chairperson - Former Vice President at BioNTech leading External Innovations and APAC/China Development; prior equity research experience at major banks; M.D. (Peking University), Ph.D. (UC Irvine), MBA (MIT).
  • Thang Ho, Ph.D., Co‑Founder and Chief Development Officer - Former Clinical Pharmacology and Pharmacometrics Lead at BioNTech; prior roles at Takeda, Vertex, and CytomX; Ph.D. in Chemical Engineering (University of Pittsburgh).
  • Jonathan I. Lieber, M.B.A., Chief Financial Officer - Former CFO at Applied Genetic Technologies and Histogenics; Managing Director at Danforth Advisors; investment banking background; MBA (NYU Stern).
  • Crystal MacKay, Chief Operating Officer - Former Director of Healthcare Investment Banking at BTIG; prior operational and finance roles in diagnostics; B.A. in Business Communications (UMass).

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: Bambusa Therapeutics, Inc.
  • Filing date: October 09, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: BBTX
  • Exchange: Nasdaq Global Select Market
  • Lead underwriters: BofA Securities, Evercore ISI, UBS Investment Bank, Cantor
  • Use of proceeds: Fund continued development of BBT001 (including Phase 2b AD study) and BBT002 (including a Phase 2b respiratory indication study); advance BBT003 and BBT004; and for capital expenditures, working capital, and general corporate purposes.

data.title: Anthropic AI Model Goes Rogue, Submits Fake Unsolved Murder Tip — WSJ
data.description:
By Georgia Wells and Joseph Pisani

Rogue AI models have hacked companies and tried to break into government websites. Now they are submitting fake tips for unsolved crimes.

Police in Philadelphia say Anthropic alerted it this week that one of its artificial-intelligence models submitted a false homicide tip through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com. The incident happened in July. Anthropic didn't realize it until September.

"The City of Philadelphia takes this incident very seriously," the police department said. "The two-month delay in detecting and reporting the incident to the city is unacceptable."

Anthropic's model was conducting a test involving interactions with randomly selected websites when it submitted the tip pretending to be someone who might have information about an unsolved case, police said.

The submission, dated July 18, went to spam and was never sent for further investigation. That doesn't take away from the seriousness of what happened, police said.

"Unsolved cases involve real victims, grieving families and investigators working to secure answers," the department said. "Technology companies must take all appropriate steps necessary to prevent their systems from submitting false information to law enforcement."

Anthropic told the Philadelphia police that the company discovered the incident on Sept. 28, and terminated the automated testing process responsible for the submission, the department said. Anthropic also told the police it added an additional validation mechanism for future testing, according to the agency.

Anthropic notified the Philadelphia police on Oct. 7, nine days after discovering the incident. Police said the company met with the department the next day.

Anthropic didn't respond to requests for comment.

Anthropic has previously alerted police departments to more substantive information about potential risks. In late September, the sheriff's office in Florida's Lee County arrested a woman after a tip from Anthropic. The woman had made statements that she would "shoot up" the county's sheriff's office, according to the arrest report.

AI companies haven't always alerted law enforcement to potential risks. In February, Canadian law enforcement named Jesse Van Rootselaar as the suspect in the Tumbler Ridge mass shooting, months after OpenAI employees had considered alerting law enforcement about Van Rootselaar's interactions with the company's chatbot. OpenAI ultimately decided not to contact authorities, and the company now faces a lawsuit from British Columbia as well as dozens of victims.

PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com, where the fake tip was sent in, is a Philadelphia police website that lists unsolved homicides, takes tips on cases and offers a $20,000 reward for information that leads to an arrest.

"Members of the public should continue to submit legitimate information about unsolved homicides through PhillyUnsolvedMurders.com," the police said.

data.title: Oil Futures Settle Modestly Higher — Market Talk
data.description:

Concerns remained about continued attacks on shipping in the Middle East and loss of U.S. production to Hurricane Isaias. "The prospect of easing tensions still needs to be reinforced by concrete progress in negotiations and improvements in shipping safety through the Strait of Hormuz," Linh Tran of XS.com says in a note. 1559 ET - Treasury yields slip as the bonds selloff ease to end another eventful week ahead of key U.S. inflation data. September CPI is due Wednesday, two weeks before the Fed's expected hold. Long-dated yields climb down from fresh 24-year highs after investors flock to Treasury auctions that pay the highest yields in a quarter-century. President Trump announces a deal with Russia to supply diesel to global markets in an effort to ease energy inflation. Trump also renews the push to oust Fed's Lisa Cook, reviving concerns about central bank independence. The 10-year yield slips 0.033 percentage point to 5.243% this week. The two-year drops 0.034 point to 4.789%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1526 ET - Hong Kong-based NFT Ltd. is small in size but ranks high for statistics like recent trading halts. The company formerly known as Takung Art operates an art sale platform and is exploring sectors including NFT gaming. After posting five-digit trading volume for most of September, shares become more active. On Monday, the stock rose 683% to $7 and the company said it was "not aware of any undisclosed information or business development that it believes would account for the trading activity." Shares fell 82% Tuesday. The week included three announcements of registered direct offerings, three trading halts for news pending and several brief pauses due to volatility. Friday's volume recently topped 41 million, below Monday's 166.9 million but above Tuesday-through-Thursday figures. (josh.beckerman@wsj.com)

1511 ET - United Airlines flyers will be able to watch almost every MLB playoff game via DISH streaming supported by Starlink, the connectivity business of Elon Musk's SpaceX. United's Friday announcement comes Delta CEO Ed Bastian doubled-down on his decision not to use Starlink for inflight Wi-Fi in an interview with The Wall Street Journal. United says it is offering a status match offer for members of Delta and American Airlines loyalty programs. "Quality inflight Wi-Fi is more important than ever to travelers, and because Starlink gives people the same — or better — connectivity in the sky than they can get at home, it's a reason to choose United," the company says. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1358 ET - Sub-Saharan African sovereigns are being supported by economic reforms and generally favorable access to external financing, leading to an improved rating profile in the region, Fitch Ratings says. Revenue-enhancing measures and spending rationalization are leading to improved fiscal performance, Fitch says, adding it expects the median sovereign in the region will record a primary fiscal surplus this year. The region's rating profile has continued to improve, with the average sovereign rating now at its highest level since the pandemic, according to Fitch. It adds that the share of sovereigns with Positive Outlooks is at a decade high, pointing to the potential for further rating improvements. (stephen.nakrosis@wsj.com)

1349 ET - The sell-off in AT&T, Verizon, and T-Mobile US following SpaceX's deal to buy cellular spectrum licenses from investment firm Grain Management, may be overstating the competitive risks of SpaceX's mobile network play, Morgan Stanley analysts say in a note. "The Starlink Mobile disruption story could take years to play out and, even with this addition to SpaceX's spectrum portfolio, the company won't have enough spectrum to serve as a viable standalone competitor," they say. SpaceX may be well-positioned to compete in rural areas, but the company will need to substantially up its spectrum acquisitions and invest in terrestrial infrastructure to compete in densely-populated urban areas. T-Mobile slides 13%, AT&T falls 10%, and Verizon drops 9.8%. SpaceX is up 0.5%. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1310 ET - The recent riot in global bond markets still leaves many opportunities for fixed-income investors. "We are still happy to be there," F/m Investments' Alex Morris says. There are "a lot of high-rated [corporate bonds] that may actually be a better credit risk in some sense than some domestic economy sovereign debt." He's staying away from hyperscalers' debt as they have multiplied and "it's hard to really pick the good from the bad." Morris expects long-term rates to come down, likely in 2027. He adds that rising government spending poses a long-term risk for bonds. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1307 ET - Xerox will have to execute against a challenging backdrop in the print market if it wants to reach sustainable revenue growth and stronger core free cash flow, Citi analysts write in a note, downgrading the stock to sell. Though the company has made progress on integrating its acquisition of Lexmark, they write, that acquisition and other management efforts may not be sufficient to offset pressures in the cash generation of Xerox's core business. "Until Xerox demonstrates sustained organic revenue stabilization alongside margin expansion, stronger normalized FCF and meaningful deleveraging, we see an unfavorable risk/reward, supporting our Sell rating," the analysts write. Shares fall 6.8% to $2.72. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1246 ET - Tilray Brands still has work to do in its legacy beverage and adult-use cannabis business, but there are green shoots of improvement, according to TD Cowen's Derek Lessard. In a report, the analyst notes that the company is making progress against its key priorities, and that "we are encouraged by the early performance of its new cannabis strains, alongside improving BrewDog demand and margins." It is still early days for these new additions. "While these trends are still developing, they give us greater confidence in TLRY's longer-term growth outlook," Lessard says. He expects recreational cannabis to return to growth in 2H, while the recent acquisition of BrewDog should help lift overall margins above its legacy average. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

1234 ET - The USDA increases its estimate for cotton production in the 2026/27 marketing year amid larger crops in Delta states. The October WASDE report projects output at 13.44 million bales, up from 13.20 million bales in the September forecast. Ending stocks increase to 3.8 million from 3.6 million bales. World production estimate is also raised, to 117.95 million from 117.32 million bales. The front-month cotton contract pares down losses after the report and slips 0.2%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1232 ET - U.S. beef production outlook is lowered in the October WASDE report, due to lighter dressed weights and lower-than-expected feedlot placements. The USDA projects 2027 beef production at 24.7 billion pounds, down from September's projection of 24.8 billion pounds. Steer prices are unchanged at $2.38 a pound. Pork output is now expected to be 27.8 billion pounds, down from 28.1 billion pounds in the previous projection. Barrows and gilts price estimate slips to 63 from 64 cents a pound. The front-month live cattle contract rises 0.7%, while lean hogs fall 1%, both little changed from before the report. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1230 ET - Aritzia gave investors the earnings beat they wanted, says Irene Nattel of RBC. In a report, she notes that Ebitda doubled year-over-year, which was 23% above forecast "by stronger than forecast revenues across geographies and channels and better than forecast gross margins and SG&A leverage." She says that this was backed by existing customer loyalty and successful new customer acquisition through strong product, effective marketing strategies, geographic expansion and accelerating digital growth. "ATZ delivered another exceptional quarter in ways in which investors should want to see," she says. The momentum is carrying over into 3Q, with the upper end of the quarter's guidance 6% above prior forecast. Shares are up 15% to C$140.44. (adriano.marchese@wsj.com)

Power infrastructure firm Base Electron said on Friday it had confidentially filed for a U.S. initial public offering.

The confidential filing comes as interest in AI-linked infrastructure remains strong, though investors are increasingly scrutinising valuations, capital needs and backlog quality.

data.title: Gran Tierra Energy Inc. Stockholders Approve Sale of Colombian and Ecuadorian Businesses
data.description:
CALGARY, Alberta, Oct. 09, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Gran Tierra Energy Inc. (“Gran Tierra” or the “Company”) (NYSE American:GTE) today announced that its stockholders have approved the previously announced sale of Gran Tierra’s Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses to Maurel & Prom for total consideration of approximately US$1.33 billion, including the assumption of debt and subject to adjustment (the “Sale”). The vote took place at the Company’s special meeting of stockholders held on October 9, 2026 (the “Special Meeting”). The Sale is to be effected pursuant to the Share Sale and Purchase Agreement entered into on August 5, 2026 (the “Share Purchase Agreement”). Gran Tierra expects to receive total net cash proceeds from the Sale of approximately US$315 million, of which approximately US$250 million is payable on closing and approximately US$65 million is payable 364 days thereafter.

“We thank our stockholders for their support of the Sale,” said Gary Guidry, President and Chief Executive Officer of Gran Tierra. “Today’s approval moves us a step closer to closing a transaction that realizes value for our Colombian and Ecuadorian businesses. On closing, Gran Tierra expects to be debt free, with the flexibility to return capital to stockholders and fund our Canadian and Azerbaijan portfolios.”

Special Meeting Results: Based on the final report of the independent inspector of election, the voting results for each of the proposals considered at the Special Meeting are set out below. Final voting results will also be reported in a Current Report on Form 8-K to be filed with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (the “SEC”).

ProposalForAgainstAbstainBroker Non-Votes
1. Approval of the Sale19,351,11532,4927,3280
2. Advisory Non-Binding Approval of Sale-Related Named Executive Officer Compensation9,557,0079,658,068175,8600
3. Adjournment of the Special Meeting19,304,19662,74223,9970

Closing of the Sale: With stockholder approval and the requisite consents of the holders of the Company’s 9.750% Senior Secured Amortizing Notes due 2031 now obtained, the remaining conditions to closing include the regulatory approvals in Colombia and Ecuador and other customary closing conditions. Completion of the Sale remains subject to the satisfaction or waiver of these and the other closing conditions set out in the Share Purchase Agreement, as described in the Company’s definitive proxy statement filed on September 15, 2026. Gran Tierra continues to target closing of the Sale on or about December 31, 2026. As previously announced, the Company expects to use a portion of the net cash proceeds from the Sale to return capital to stockholders through a share repurchase, the structure, size and terms of which will be determined by the Board of Directors and announced separately. Any share repurchase is conditional on completion of the Sale.

Contact Information

For investor and media inquiries please contact:

Gary Guidry, Chief Executive Officer

Ryan Ellson, Executive Vice President & Chief Financial Officer

(403) 265-3221

info@grantierra.com

About Gran Tierra Energy Inc.Gran Tierra Energy Inc., together with its subsidiaries, is an independent international energy company currently focused on oil and natural gas exploration and production in Canada, Colombia and Ecuador. The Company is the operator of, and holds a 65% working interest in, an onshore exploration, development and production sharing agreement in Azerbaijan. Upon completion of the Sale, the Company’s operations will be focused on Canada and Azerbaijan, and the Company will continue to pursue additional new growth opportunities that would further strengthen the Company’s portfolio. The Company’s common stock trades on the NYSE American, the Toronto Stock Exchange and the London Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol GTE. Additional information concerning Gran Tierra is available at www.grantierra.com. Except to the extent expressly stated otherwise, information on the Company’s website or accessible from our website or any other website is not incorporated by reference into and should not be considered part of this press release. data.title: TRex Bio, Clinical-Stage Immunology Biopharma, Files for Nasdaq Global Select Market IPO
data.description:
TRex Bio filed a final prospectus for its initial public offering, pricing 8,333,334 shares at $14.00 per share. The company has been approved to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker “TRXB,” with gross proceeds expected to be approximately $116.7 million before underwriting discounts and expenses. Underwriters have a 30‑day option to purchase up to 1,250,000 additional shares, and Eli Lilly has indicated interest in purchasing shares to hold up to 19.9% post‑offering.

Business Description

TRex Bio is a clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company developing immunoregulatory medicines that aim to restore immune balance and promote tissue repair by targeting regulatory T cells (Tregs) in diseased tissues. Built on its proprietary Deep Biology platform, the company identifies and validates targets that augment tissue Tregs, linking human tissue insights with translational strategies to guide drug design and development.

Its lead wholly owned candidate, TRB-061, is a selective TNFR2 agonist designed to expand and activate Tregs in inflamed tissues. TRB-061 is in a Phase 1b study in patients with moderate-to-severe atopic dermatitis, with topline data expected in mid‑2027, and potential expansion into alopecia areata. The second program, TRB-071, is a CD30 agonist antibody intended to both activate Tregs and modulate inflammatory signaling, with a Phase 1 trial planned for the first half of 2027. Beyond its wholly owned pipeline, TRex Bio has a collaboration with Eli Lilly that originated TRB-051, which Lilly is advancing, including plans for a Phase 2a study in lupus with cutaneous involvement.

Market Overview

  • Total addressable market: Atopic dermatitis impacts ~16 million U.S. adults and ~225 million people globally; IBD affects ~3 million Americans and is expected to exceed 10 million patients worldwide by 2032.
  • Market growth: Rising prevalence of immune-mediated diseases and continued biologics/small‑molecule adoption support sustained category growth.
  • Market position: Early-stage clinical company focused on tissue regulatory T cell (Treg) biology with a platform designed to discover and develop immunoregulatory therapies.
  • Key competitors: Existing AD and IBD treatments from large and specialty pharma (e.g., IL-4/13 inhibitors such as dupilumab; JAK inhibitors), and emerging Treg‑modulating approaches.
  • Industry trends: Shift from broad immunosuppression toward targeted immunoregulation; increasing interest in Treg augmentation and tissue‑repair mechanisms.

Operational Metrics

  • Customers: Not applicable; company is pre-commercial
  • Locations: Headquarters and labs in South San Francisco, California
  • Geographic presence: United States-focused operations and clinical development
  • Partnerships: Strategic collaboration with Eli Lilly; TRB-051 originated from TRex platform and is being advanced by Lilly
  • Orders/GMV: Not applicable
  • Other key metrics: Approximately 60 full-time employees as of August 31, 2026; cash runway projected into the second half of 2029 per use-of-proceeds plan

Financials Highlights

  • Revenue (current): 2025 revenue: $0 (2024: $39.1 million collaboration revenue)
  • Revenue growth: Down from $39.1 million in 2024 to $0 in 2025 as collaboration revenue recognition concluded
  • Net income: Net loss: $(34.8) million in 2025; $(29.3) million for the six months ended June 30, 2026

Management

  • M. Johnston Erwin, Jr., Chief Executive Officer and Chair - Over 40 years in pharma leadership at Eli Lilly; led Lilly New Ventures and prior global regulatory submissions for Evista and Forteo.
  • Laura Berner, JD, MBA, Chief Operating Officer - 25 years in strategy, corporate development, and legal; prior roles at Myovant, Roche/Genentech; leads business and corporate development.
  • Brandon Hants, MBA, Chief Financial Officer - 25+ years in biotech finance; former CFO at Applied Molecular Transport; prior roles at Singulex, Novartis Vaccines & Diagnostics, and Genentech.
  • Ariella Kelman, MD, Chief Medical Officer - 20+ years in immunology clinical development; previously at Biora and Genentech/Roche; former attending physician at Stanford University.
  • Ali Zarrin, PhD, Chief Scientific Officer - 25+ years in immunology and translational R&D led development of TRex’s Deep Biology platform; former Genentech R&D leader.

IPO Structure

  • Issuer: TRex Bio, Inc.
  • Filing date: October 09, 2026
  • Proposed ticker: TRXB
  • Exchange: Nasdaq Global Select Market
  • Price range: $14.00 per share
  • Offering size: $116,666,676 gross proceeds
  • Shares offered: 8,333,334 shares (plus 1,250,000 over-allotment option)
  • Lead underwriters: J.P. Morgan; Evercore ISI; Cantor; Stifel; Wedbush PacGrow
  • Use of proceeds: Approximately $103.5 million net to fund Phase 2 trials of TRB-061 in atopic dermatitis and alopecia areata through topline data, initiate and complete a Phase 1 trial of TRB-071 in healthy volunteers, and for working capital and general corporate purposes.

data.title: Starbucks and Chipotle: Why Wall Street Finds the Combo Unappetizing — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Evie Liu

A potential Starbucks takeover of Chipotle Mexican Grill could create one of the world's biggest restaurant companies, one that would serve everything from iced lattes to pork burritos. But Wall Street isn't convinced it's a good idea.

A merger of the two chains would be expensive, bring many challenges to management, and disrupt Starbucks' turnaround. What's more, Chipotle may not want to sell, especially when analysts believe its stock has plenty of room to recover on its own.

The questions arise after The Financial Times reported Thursday that Starbucks is working with advisors on a possible takeover of Chipotle, potentially reuniting CEO Brian Niccol with the burrito chain he once led.

No offer has been confirmed. Starbucks told Barron's that it remains "laser focused" on executing its Back to Starbucks turnaround strategy. Chipotle didn't immediately respond to a request for comment.

The strategic appeal of the deal is understandable.

Chipotle would give Starbucks another source of growth beyond coffee and beverages, while extending its reach further into lunch and dinner, said D.A. Davidson analyst Matt Curtis. The fast-casual chain also has substantial room to grow, with more than 4,200 restaurants and a long-term target of 7,000 locations in North America

Curtis notes that the two chains serve similar customer groups in the U.S. By combining customer data and linking their rewards programs, they could offer targeted promotions to drive more traffic and sales for each other.

Starbucks' extensive international network could help Chipotle expand overseas, but the potential benefits may be limited, said Raymond James's Brian Vaccaro. He noted that Chipotle already works with some of Starbucks' major overseas operators in the Middle East and Latin America, raising questions about how much additional help Starbucks could provide.

The two companies have little overlap in their supply chains, limiting opportunities to cut costs. Starbucks primarily sources coffee and prepared food, while Chipotle buys fresh ingredients from farms.

Sharon Zackfia, an analyst at William Blair, estimates that combining corporate operations and technology could save roughly $300 million annually.

Unlike other restaurant mergers involving largely franchised chains, a Starbucks-Chipotle combination would bring together two businesses that generate much of their U.S. profits from company-operated locations, which adds significantly more complexity, wrote Seaport Research Partners' Eric Gonzalez.

Starbucks is still working through its own turnaround, and adding another major restaurant business could distract management from those efforts.

"We wonder about the team's ability to handle the complexities and demands of both businesses simultaneously," wrote Gonzalez in a Thursday note.

Meanwhile, Curtis questioned whether it's a good choice for Starbucks to diversify away from beverages — one of the fastest-growing restaurant categories — into food, which generally offers lower profit margins than beverages. That means an acquisition could weigh on the combined company's profitability.

The biggest obstacle, however, may be the price.

Zackfia estimates an acquisition could cost nearly $50 billion, assuming a premium of about 20%. Starbucks already had about $9.4 billion in net debt at the end of June, according to Zackfia, borrowing enough to finance the purchase would push Starbucks' debt to an unusually high level for a publicly traded restaurant company.

The company has paused share buybacks, sold a majority stake in its China business and used part of the proceeds to repay debt, and is reportedly exploring a sale of its Japan operations. A major acquisition would represent a sharp reversal from those efforts to simplify its business and strengthen its balance sheet, wrote TD Cowen analyst Andrew Charles.

Paying with Starbucks shares would be more realistic, Curtis told Barron's. Rather than borrowing tens of billions of dollars, Starbucks could issue new shares to Chipotle shareholders. That would avoid taking on substantial additional debt, but issuing new shares would dilute existing Starbucks shareholders' ownership in the combined company.

Rather than relying entirely on either option, Starbucks could use a combination of stock and debt to fund the purchase, said Vaccaro.

Chipotle shares have fallen 15% this year amid concerns about consumer spending and rising operating costs. Its restaurant-level profit margin fell to 25.2% in the second quarter from 27.4% a year earlier, although same-store sales growth accelerated to 2.2% from 0.5% in the previous quarter.

But Wall Street generally believes the stock is oversold. Two thirds of the analysts polled by FactSet have a Buy rating for Chipotle stock, with an average target price of $44. The stock closed Thursday at $32.68. Curtis, for one, believes Chipotle has substantial room to recover on its own, with a target price of $50.

Chipotle's weaker share price could make it an attractive acquisition target for Starbucks. Even a 20% takeover premium to Thursday's close would value Chipotle at just $39 a share, below the average analyst target. That could make shareholders reluctant to accept an offer that undervalues its long-term prospects.

A higher acquisition premium, however, would make an already expensive transaction even harder for Starbucks to justify. Curtis estimates the likelihood of a completed deal at just 20%.

"If synergies are not the primary motivation, then a key question for Brian Niccol would be what he would do differently than Chipotle's current management team," wrote Gonzalez.

Write to Evie Liu at evie.liu@barrons.com

This content was created by Barron's, which is operated by Dow Jones & Co. Barron's is published independently from Dow Jones Newswires and The Wall Street Journal.

data.title: GTCR, Elliott in advanced talks to acquire CCC Intelligent Solutions, Bloomberg News reports
data.description:
Private equity firm GTCR and activist investor Elliott Investment Management are in advanced talks to acquire software provider CCC Intelligent Solutions , Bloomberg News reported on Friday, citing people familiar with the matter.

A deal could be announced as soon as next week, however, a final agreement had not been reached, the report said, without disclosing financial details.

Shares of the company, which provides software for auto insurance firms, rose about 10% in extended trading.

CCC, Elliott and GTCR did not immediately respond to Reuters' requests for comment.

Bloomberg News had reported in August that online vehicle auctioneer Copart was in talks to acquire CCC Intelligent Solutions, which has been exploring a sale.

data.title: CFTC Proposes to Expand Definition of Swaps to Include Prediction Markets Trading
data.description:
By Katherine Hamilton

The Commodity Futures Trading Commission is proposing to provide what it describes as additional clarity on the term "swap" that would include event contracts used in prediction market trading.

The expanded term would encompass event contracts on sporting, political, cultural and weather-related events, the CFTC said in a statement Friday.

The proposal notes that event contracts are financial instruments commonly known to trade as swaps.

The prediction markets industry, which is regulated by the CFTC, has been enmeshed in a debate about whether trading on events constitutes gambling, which would put it under the legal purview of states. The CFTC has said that the emerging industry is a form of financial trading, not betting.

"These products are commodity derivatives squarely within the CFTC's regulatory remit under the Commodity Exchange Act and are within the agency's exclusive jurisdiction," CFTC Chair Michael Selig said.

The agency is seeking public comment on the proposal. Comments must be submitted within 30 days.

Write to Katherine Hamilton at katherine.hamilton@wsj.com

data.title: S&P maintains UK's ratings as economy weathers Middle East energy shock
data.description:
S&P retained the UK's sovereign rating at "AA/A-1+" with a "stable" outlook on Friday, citing the economy's resilience despite the energy shock stemming from the Middle East conflict.

Britain's economy expanded faster than previously estimated in the second quarter, cementing its position as the fastest-growing economy in the Group of Seven in the first half of 2026.

"Despite the conflict in the Middle East, reasonably resilient consumer spending and services, particularly hospitality and professional services, supported second-quarter growth," the global ratings agency said in a statement.

Reflecting the stronger-than-expected economic performance in the first half of this year, S&P raised its 2026 growth forecast for Britain to 1.3% and expects growth to average 1.4% in 2027-2029.

The affirmation comes as the new government under Andy Burnham seeks to reshape economic policy amid mounting fiscal pressures and higher borrowing costs.

In September, Burnham said he knew he had to show investors he had faced "up to the reality" of the public finances in order to stabilise markets, before he can make bigger changes to the economy.

Finance Minister John Healey also faces pressure to find billions of pounds in his October 28 budget to offset rising debt-servicing costs, while funding Burnham's plans for expanded social care and higher defence spending.

S&P said while parliamentary majority gives Burnham latitude to pursue his policy agenda, there have been significant cost-of-living shocks to contend with, and expenditure plans will have to be balanced against revenue limitations and the risk of curtailing GDP growth due to an excessively high tax burden.

data.title: Niki BioSolutions Launches $1.396 Million ATM Equity Program With H.C. Wainwright
data.description:
Niki BioSolutions entered into an At the Market Offering Agreement to sell up to $1.396 million of common stock from time to time through H.C. Wainwright as sales agent, with Brookline Capital Markets acting as qualified independent underwriter due to a conflict. Sales will occur at prevailing market prices, and Wainwright will receive a 3.0% placement fee. The company and agents may suspend or terminate the program at any time. The arrangement provides flexible access to equity financing.

Agreement details:

  • Agreement type: At-the-market equity offering program for common stock
  • Counterparty: H.C. Wainwright; Brookline Capital Markets
  • Signed / Effective: Oct 09 2026 / Oct 09 2026
  • Duration / Termination: At will
  • Reason: Flexibly raise equity capital

Original SEC Filing: Niki BioSolutions, Inc. [ NIKI ] - 8-K - Oct. 09, 2026
